subject: US-Central tiered failover brief: temporary model capacity fallback
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: US-Central P95/5xx spike — automatic tiered failover triggered

Team,

We started seeing elevated 5xx rates and sustained p95 latency increases in the us-central cluster at ~08:45 PDT. Our routing layer automatically began routing a subset of requests to the tiered fallback pool (lower-capacity model variant) at 08:52 to preserve overall throughput. Observable impact:
- 5xx rate peaked at 3.4% for ~22 minutes, now down to ~0.4%.
- Requests routed to fallback saw median latency increase from 120ms -> 410ms and occasional truncated streams.

Initial cause signal points to a recent kernel rollout on the us-central inference nodes that increased memory pressure for long-sequence requests. QA rollout was green but the traffic profile in us-central exposed KV cache churn.

Attachments: usc-failover-metrics.csv (sampling of metrics), incident-timeline.pdf (rough timeline).

Immediate asks:
- Marissa: can you confirm capacity throttles and whether we can raise burst pool for affected customers?
- Aditya: can you gate the kernel rollout and prepare a rollback?
- Irene: I recommend we craft a short customer note for affected accounts, call out mitigation and ETA.

Ben
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@stellarmedia.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia@stellarmedia.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: US-Central tiered failover brief: temporary model capacity fallback

Sam / Olivia —

Short version: we detected an infrastructure regression in US-Central that caused a subset of inference traffic to be routed to a fallback model variant. This produced higher latency and a small number of 5xx responses for approximately 20–30 minutes this morning. The team triggered an automatic failover to protect throughput, then deployed a targeted rollback to the prior kernel at 09:20 PDT which restored normal routing.

What we did for Stellar Media (what matters to you):
- Incident window: ~08:45–09:20 PDT (partial impact).
- Customer-visible effects: occasional slower responses and intermittent 5xx for a small subset of burst requests. We do not believe any inference results were corrupted; all model outputs were valid.
- Current status: service healthy for your account; we are monitoring.

Next steps we will take and commitments:
- A postmortem and timeline will be shared by 2028-04-13 with root cause and remediation items.
- We will propose a one-time usage credit for impacted tokens in the incident window; I will route approval with finance and include an explicit credit amount in the postmortem.
- We’ll add an additional check in the kernel rollout pipeline to simulate high KV churn traffic for US-Central traffic profiles.

If you need a call to walk through specifics, I’m available this afternoon 2–4pm PDT. Otherwise I’ll follow up with the postmortem link and proposed credit amount.

Thanks for bearing with this — apologies for the interruption.

— Irene
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@stellarmedia.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: US-Central tiered failover brief: temporary model capacity fallback — postmortem & customer follow-up

Team,

Postmortem summary (for inclusion in the public postmortem and customer-facing note):
- Root cause: a kernel optimization rollout (commit 9f4a...) increased KV eviction pressure for long-context sequences on us-central nodes. This caused cascading latency for requests that hit large KV caches and triggered the routing policy to divert traffic to fallback model variants.
- Impact: ~25 minutes of elevated p95 and a peak 5xx rate of 3.4% in US-Central. Affected customers experienced higher latency and a small number of 5xx responses. No data loss or incorrect outputs were detected.
- Mitigation timeline: detection 08:45 PDT; automatic tiered failover 08:52 PDT; rollback and routing restore 09:20 PDT; monitoring green 09:40 PDT.

Action items:
- Aditya: block the problematic kernel commit in the rollout pipeline and add a new high-KV-churn simulation to pre-release tests.
- Marissa: add a capability to temporarily expand the dedicated burst pool for accounts flagged as high-priority to avoid fallback routing while we repair infra. Create the runbook entry: RINF-4427.
- Ben: publish the cleaned metrics attachment and a short annotated timeline for the customer postmortem.
- Irene: finalize customer credit proposal and publish the postmortem to both the status page and the customer portal by 2028-04-13.

Customer follow-up status: Sam asked for token counts and credit mechanics; Marissa to estimate affected tokens (approx. range) and Ben to prepare metrics table for the credit calculation. I will route the credit approval through finance once we have the numbers.

References: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-04-10-usc-failover (public incident), https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-4427 (internal runbook).

Irene
